messages:
Devon Price: heads up: I’m updating the postmortem template to include the new incident taxonomy fields. Need quick alignment on (a) required vs optional fields, (b) what to do w/ `unknown`, (c) who reviews classification accuracy.

Devon Price: draft template WIP (Confluence): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/x/postmortem-template-taxonomy-wip

Rafael Mendes: +1, let’s make this crisp. Goal is: every Sev0/Sev1 postmortem is reportable by type/owner without arguing later.

Kira Thompson: can we keep the required section small? people already hate filling these out at 2am.

Allison Grant: also reminder: the template drives metrics labels + dashboards. we should enforce allowlist + no freeform incident_type.

Devon Price: current proposal for REQUIRED fields in the template (top of doc):
- incident_type (allowlist dropdown)
- incident_subtype (dropdown, but only required for certain types)
- customer_tier impacted (Hosted/Dedicated/Private/Multiple)
- severity (Sev0-3)
- primary_owner_team (auto-filled from mapping but editable w/ reason)
- contributing_systems (multi-select, freeform text ok)
- remediation_sla: met/breached + time_to_mitigate + time_to_fix
- links: incident channel + timeline doc + dashboards

Devon Price: optional:
- contributing_factors flags (provider_outage, rollout_regression, security_flag)
- classification_confidence (high/med/low)

Aisha Bello: re SLA fields: for postmortem we should capture the *policy outcome* (met/breached/paused) + the timestamps we use to compute it.
Aisha Bello: otherwise folks will handwave “met” and it won’t match the evaluator.

Dylan Brooks: for incident-bot we already have start/mitigated/resolved timestamps. template should just reference those + any pause/override reason.

Mei Lin: +1. and we should explicitly say “incident_type = impact surface, not root cause”. otherwise folks will put “provider outage” as the type.

Rafael Mendes: agree. incident_type should be the impact bucket (availability/latency/streaming/etc). provider/rollout/security should be contributing flags.

Sofia Ivanova: pls add note: don’t use telemetry_blind_spot as the primary if customers had actual 5xx/latency. telemetry can be contributing.

Devon Price: ack, adding guidance callout.

Kira Thompson: question: for incident_subtype, can we avoid making it required across the board? i’m worried it becomes another debate.

Rafael Mendes: proposal: subtype required only when it changes owner/escalation.
Rafael Mendes: e.g. Routing: {fallback_loop, wrong_target, routing_timeout}. Capacity: {region_saturation, provisioning_lag}. Private: {dns_tls, network_path, config_upgrade}.

Allison Grant: +1. also keep subtype out of metric labels for now. template can have it; dashboards can group by type.

Devon Price: ok, implementing as: subtype field appears for all, but required only for: routing/fallback, capacity/fleet, private connectivity. others optional.

Elliot Price: from training/docs POV, we should add “Good vs Bad examples” right under the required fields.
Elliot Price: ex: “Customers getting 500s because router stuck in fallback loop” => type=Availability, subtype=(optional) throttle/overload? hmm, that one’s tricky.

Rafael Mendes: careful: if customers getting 500s, type=Availability. routing can be contributing_system or contributing_flag.
Rafael Mendes: if the primary operational issue is router picking wrong target (causing failures even with capacity), then type=Routing/Fallback Misbehavior (even if symptom is 5xx). that’s exactly what decision tree is for.

Mei Lin: yep, decision tree should be referenced from template: “If unsure, follow decision tree; default to impact bucket; update later.”

Devon Price: ok now the `unknown` policy.
Devon Price: current text: “`unknown` allowed during incident + initial postmortem draft, but MUST be updated before postmortem is marked ‘Reviewed’ (or within 24h of resolve, whichever is earlier). If still unknown, include: what evidence is missing + tracking ticket.”

Kira Thompson: can we loosen for Sev2/Sev3? sometimes we never do a full postmortem.

Rafael Mendes: for Sev2/Sev3 (no postmortem), incident record still needs a type before close. for the template specifically, scope is Sev0/Sev1 postmortems.

Allison Grant: +1. and please add: `unknown` is not a permanent category. it’s an escalation signal that decision tree didn’t work.

Aisha Bello: also add a reason code for unknown (like “insufficient telemetry”, “multiple plausible causes”, “incident still ongoing”) so we can fix taxonomy gaps.

Devon Price: I can add a required short text field when unknown is selected: “unknown_reason + next step”. Not a dropdown (don’t want more taxonomy), but a sentence.

Dylan Brooks: in incident-bot we can prompt: “If unknown, set a reminder to update within 24h” and ping IC + owner.

Incident Bot: Reminder set by Devon Price: “Update incident_type from unknown within 24h (or before Reviewed).”

Elliot Price: who’s the reviewer for classification accuracy? is it the postmortem reviewer or SRE program?

Rafael Mendes: ownership model I’d like:
- IC (or on-call lead) sets initial incident_type during incident
- primary_owner_team validates/updates during postmortem draft
- SRE reviewer checks taxonomy correctness as part of postmortem review (lightweight)

Mei Lin: +1. but we should have a periodic audit too. reviewers are inconsistent.

Aisha Bello: I can take a weekly “taxonomy QA” sweep for Sev0/Sev1: sample 5-10 incidents, check type/owner alignment vs decision tree, report gaps.

Allison Grant: and if we see repeated misclassifications, we update the decision tree / template examples rather than policing people.

Kira Thompson: can we document the “if disputed” process? sometimes owner mapping is political.

Rafael Mendes: add a line: “If incident_type/owner disputed, default to decision tree result; escalate to #eng-sre with link; Rafael (SRE) is tie-breaker for v1.”

Devon Price: ok.

Devon Price: last question: should we block “Reviewed” status if incident_type is unknown / blank?

Dylan Brooks: yes for Sev0/Sev1. otherwise we’ll never clean it up.

Allison Grant: +1, but ensure it’s not blocking on subtype unless it’s one of the required types.

Sofia Ivanova: +1. also please make “contributing_systems” required; that helps avoid blaming runtime when it’s routing/capacity.

Devon Price: done. contributing_systems required (freeform list ok).

Elliot Price: I’ll add 3-4 examples to the template + link to the “Incident taxonomy v1 definitions” page once it’s published.

Devon Price: cool. I’ll push the template update today and share for final review here. action items:
- Devon: implement required fields + unknown gating for “Reviewed”
- Rafael: add dispute/tie-breaker language + unknown policy wording
- Aisha: weekly taxonomy QA sweep process (1 pager)
- Elliot: examples section + training note

Rafael Mendes: :thumbsup: thanks. this is one of those annoying changes that pays off fast when dashboards stop being junk.

Kira Thompson: 👍 as long as it doesn’t become “fill out 30 fields” lol

Devon Price: promise: boring v1, minimal fields. will ping when ready for sign-off.
